title: Question item
description: One chemistry fact (start + route + product) with everything needed to present it as several order types. The engine chooses an order type from `orderTypes`; the validator checks that each listed type has the sections it needs. Molecules are SMILES only; RDKit draws them at runtime.

reactionId.description: Primary reaction this item drills. Multi-step items list the others in `reactionIds`.

reactionIds.description: All reactions involved (multistep specials). Mastery is logged for each.

orderTypes.description: Order types this item may be served as. Requirements per type: make_it -> start, route, answer, productDistractors(>=3); predict_product -> start, route, answer, productDistractors(>=3); find_start -> start, route, answer, startDistractors(>=3); name_it -> answer.names; spot_flaw -> flaw; multistep -> route with >=2 steps and reactionIds.

start.description: Starting material handed over by the customer.

alt.description: Other routes graded as fully correct for THIS item (in addition to the reaction's altRoutes).

smiles.description: Major product. Several molecules are dot-separated (LiAlH4 on an ester gives two alcohols).

stereoChoices.description: Options the stereo picker shows. Defaults to the reaction's usual set. Only used when stereo != none.

highlightAtoms.description: Atom indices (SMILES order) that changed, for the translucent highlight. Optional: the validator can derive them from the reaction mapping.

minor.description: Only when a minor product genuinely matters (Zaitsev vs Hofmann, o/p mixtures). Never byproducts.

productDistractors.description: Wrong products built from realistic mistakes. 3 are drawn at random for the 4-option picker.

routeDistractors.description: Flawed routes the grader matches the player's shelf picks against to choose a mistake tag. Missing workup, wrong order and missing stereo are detected automatically and need no entry.

startDistractors.description: Wrong starting materials for 'What did I start with?'.

flaw.description: Spot-the-flaw: two proposed routes to the same target; pick the one that works and tag why the other fails.

reactionId.description: Reaction that actually happens on this route (E4 for the E2 trap). Used to validate `product` with SMARTS.

product.description: What the route really gives; shown by the mentor.

choices.description: Reasons offered for 'why does the other route fail'. Exactly one must equal answer.tag.

explanation.description: 1-3 sentences the mentor says when the answer is revealed, in addition to the tag-specific 'why'.

tip.description: What the customer says on success.

source.description: Where the item comes from (textbook section, HW set, tutor drill). Chapter notes/HW win over general knowledge.

review.description: If set, the item is unsure and is listed in REVIEW.md; the engine will not serve it until the field is removed.

stereoLabel.description: none: the SMILES must carry no stereo marks. Anything else: the SMILES must carry @ or / \ marks and the picker is shown.

name.description: Display name (optional; the card shows the drawing, not the name, unless the order type asks for it).

accepted.description: All correct names: IUPAC, common, functional-class and substitutive ether names. Compared after normalisation (case, spaces, hyphens, en-dashes, commas).

traps.description: Specific wrong names with their tag. Generic slips (missing locant, alphabetical order, -al/-one, '-oxide' as an ether name) are also detected by the checker without an entry here.

why.description: 1-3 sentences the mentor says if this option is picked. Must address this specific mistake.

stereoOnly.description: true when the distractor differs from the answer only by stereochemistry (wrong enantiomer / meso vs racemic). The validator otherwise rejects distractors that match the answer with stereo stripped.

product.description: What the flawed route would actually give, if anything (shown by the mentor).
